Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: Business registration through the Orinasa platform is fully integrated with X-Road/Rahaka. The EDBM (Economic Development Board) connects to the tax directorate and statistics agencies via the platform, enabling business registration in 8 hours. Confirmed as operational.
revision_notes: World Bank blog (2022) and eGA project page confirm X-Road/Rahaka interoperability linking EDBM with the tax directorate (DGI), Ministry of Justice's commercial registry (MINJUS) and statistics institute (INSTAT) via the Orinasa business-registration ecosystem; the UGD's 2022 interoperability framework document names these same four institutions as the founding interoperable ecosystem. National interoperability was formally launched 28 April 2026 (Rahaka usage convention signed by UGD, several ministries and private-sector actors, reported by Newsmada and confirmed on INSTAT's own site), underpinned by Decree No. 2025-1959 on public information-system interoperability. Deployment remains phased/regional rather than fully nationwide (Orinasa decree of Nov 2024 confirms staged roll-out). Score of 4 (Partially integrated) confirmed against fresher evidence; not upgraded to 'Fully Integrated' given the very recent, still-expanding launch.
revised_comments: Business registration is integrated with the Rahaka/X-Road data-exchange platform: the Economic Development Board's Orinasa system exchanges data with the tax directorate (DGI), the Ministry of Justice's commercial registry (MINJUS) and the national statistics institute (INSTAT). National interoperability was formally launched in April 2026 through a Rahaka usage convention signed by the Digital Governance Unit (UGD), several ministries and INSTAT, underpinned by Decree No. 2025-1959. Roll-out remains phased and not yet nationwide, so integration is best characterised as partial.

Definition: Integration with national payment systems for government-to-person (G2P), government-to-business (G2B) transactions via data exchange
Comments: A shared government payments platform was under development to connect to Orinasa (business registration platform) and other public services. Madagascar's mobile money ecosystem (10 million users) is active. The DGU is developing a shared payment platform to avoid proliferation of multiple government payment systems.
revision_notes: The original score of 3 (Under development) rested on a 2022 World Bank blog describing a shared payment platform still being built. Since then, a November 2024 decree (No. 2024-1911) formalised dematerialised payment (card, bank transfer, mobile money) within the Orinasa business-registration platform, and the Treasury's Systeme d'Information de Gestion des Recettes Non Fiscales (SIGRNF) was officially launched in May 2025, linking government revenue collection to MVola, Orange Money and Airtel Money. SIGRNF collected roughly 59 billion ariary in Q1 2025 through a 150-entity pilot in three sites (Toamasina, Ambohidratrimo, Toliara) ahead of national roll-out. This is operational government-to-business/government digital payment integration, not merely development work, so the score is raised to 4 (Partially integrated) pending full national coverage.
revised_comments: Digital payment integration with government data exchange is partially in place. The Orinasa business-registration platform (Decree No. 2024-1911) accepts dematerialised payment by card, bank transfer and mobile money. Separately, the Treasury's SIGRNF system, launched in May 2025 in partnership with MVola, Orange Money and Airtel Money, enables mobile-money payment of non-tax government revenues (market fees, civil registration fees, passport and vehicle registration fees, and others) and is being piloted in three sites before national roll-out, having already processed about 59 billion ariary in its first quarter.

Definition: Integration of statistics, census data, administrative data for planning, M&E, and evidence-based policymaking
Comments: Statistics agencies (INSTAT) are confirmed as connected to the Rahaka/X-Road platform. This integration enables data interoperability for business registration alongside tax and commerce registry.
revision_notes: UGD's 2022 interoperability framework document explicitly names INSTAT as one of the four founding members of the Orinasa/X-Road interoperability ecosystem (alongside EDBM, DGI and MINJUS). INSTAT's own website confirms its Director-General signed the April 2026 convention formalising national Rahaka interoperability between ministries and public institutions. This supports partial integration; nationwide integration of the full statistics/planning apparatus is not yet evidenced, so the score of 4 (Partially integrated) is confirmed rather than upgraded.
revised_comments: The national statistics institute (INSTAT) is one of the founding participants in Madagascar's Rahaka/X-Road data-exchange ecosystem, alongside the tax directorate, commercial registry and business-registration platform. INSTAT's Director-General signed the April 2026 convention formalising national interoperability between ministries and public institutions, indicating operational but partial integration of statistical and administrative data for planning purposes.

revised_comments: Madagascar's tax directorate (DGI) is integrated into the Rahaka/X-Road data-exchange platform, exchanging business and taxpayer data with the commercial registry, the statistics institute and the Orinasa business-registration platform to support rapid company registration. The Treasury's SIGRNF system, launched in May 2025, further digitises non-tax revenue collection via mobile money in a phased, pilot-based roll-out. Integration of tax and revenue systems into the exchange is therefore partial but operational.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: Madagascar has a Digital Strategic Plan (PSN) 2023-2028 focused on developing telecommunications and digitizing public services. The PRODIGY project provides a comprehensive digital transformation roadmap. Public Digital co-developed the government's first digital transformation roadmap with interoperability as a key pillar. The UGD was established in 2022 as the governing entity.
revision_notes: The 2023-2028 Digital Strategic Plan (Plan Strategique National, PSN) remains the country's comprehensive digital-transformation strategy, confirmed by the US Commercial Service country guide (last updated 2025). It is reinforced by a dedicated legal framework for interoperability (Decree No. 2025-1959) and by a Digital Readiness Assessment launched with UNDP in February 2025 to refine implementation priorities across five pillars (connectivity, governance, regulation, business, human capital). Score of 4 (Comprehensive Strategy Exists) confirmed with fresher evidence.
revised_comments: Madagascar has a comprehensive government data-exchange and digital-transformation strategy, the 2023-2028 Plan Strategique National (PSN), which targets digitisation of public services and a six-percentage-point increase in the digital sector's GDP contribution by 2028. It is underpinned by a dedicated legal framework for public-sector interoperability (Decree No. 2025-1959) and refined through a Digital Readiness Assessment launched with UNDP support in February 2025, covering connectivity, governance, regulation, business environment and human capital.
